historical_notes: Developed around the Chyormoz metallurgical works, founded in 1763 and once one of the major Ural ironworks.
The old plant and part of the city were removed or inundated during creation of the Kama Reservoir; the plant closed in 1956.

Before 1917, events for residents of the factory settlement were recorded in the Nativity of the Mother of God parish registers; surrounding villages must be matched to their own parish boundaries. Factory personnel files may provide occupations and household details.

parish_history.parish: St John the Baptist Church, Ivanovskoye

historical_notes: The locality was historically two small villages: Lower Syrchikova (10 households in 1869) and Upper Syrchikova (6 households in 1869).
The name may derive from the Komi-Permyak word syrchik, meaning wagtail.
Because Syrchiki lay near Ivanovskoye in Ivanovskaya Volost, the Ivanovskoye parish is the first search target; this parish assignment is not yet proven by a surviving parish list.
